title: Benign Hematology
description: Diagnosis and treatment of non-cancerous blood disorders including anemia and clotting disorders.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Not all blood disorders are cancer. Our hematologists also diagnose and manage benign conditions such as iron deficiency anemia, vitamin B12 deficiency, inherited and acquired clotting disorders, immune thrombocytopenia, and other non-malignant hematologic conditions.

We provide thorough diagnostic workups and evidence-based management to help patients understand and treat their blood disorder effectively.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Persistent fatigue or pallor
  • Easy bruising or prolonged bleeding
  • Blood clots (DVT or PE)
  • Heavy menstrual periods
  • Recurrent nosebleeds

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
Do I need to see an oncologist for anemia?

A hematologist-oncologist can help when anemia is persistent, unexplained, or requires specialized evaluation. Many of our physicians are trained in both benign and malignant hematology.

What is a thrombophilia workup?

A series of blood tests to evaluate inherited or acquired conditions that increase your risk of blood clots, which helps guide treatment with blood thinners.

directory.description: Diagnosis and treatment of non-cancerous blood disorders including anemia and clotting disorders.

title: Bladder Cancer
description: Comprehensive bladder cancer treatment including immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and surgical interventions.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Bladder cancer ranges from superficial tumors that can be managed with outpatient procedures to muscle-invasive disease requiring aggressive multimodal treatment. Our medical oncologists work with urologic surgeons to provide a coordinated treatment approach at every stage.

Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of advanced bladder cancer, and our practice offers access to the latest checkpoint inhibitors and clinical trials.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs

  • Frequent or urgent urination
  • Pain or burning during urination
  • Pelvic pain
  • Back pain on one side

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What causes bladder cancer?

Smoking is the leading risk factor. Chemical exposures, chronic bladder infections, and certain medications also increase risk.

What is intravesical therapy?

For non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, treatment can be delivered directly into the bladder through a catheter — including BCG immunotherapy and chemotherapy.

title: Blood Cancers
description: Comprehensive care for leukemia, lymphoma, and other blood disorders with advanced treatment options.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Blood cancers encompass a broad group of malignancies including leukemias, lymphomas, and plasma cell disorders. Our hematology-oncology team has deep expertise in diagnosing and treating the full spectrum of blood cancers, from common conditions to rare subtypes.

We use advanced molecular diagnostics to precisely classify each patient's disease and match them with the most effective treatment — including novel immunotherapies, targeted agents, and clinical trials.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What is the difference between leukemia and lymphoma?

Leukemia originates in the bone marrow and blood, while lymphoma begins in the lymphatic system. Both are blood cancers but require different treatment approaches.

Do you coordinate stem cell transplants?

Yes. For patients who need stem cell transplantation, we coordinate referrals to transplant centers and manage pre- and post-transplant care locally.

title: Bone Cancers (Osteosarcomas)
description: Comprehensive bone cancer care combining chemotherapy, surgery, and emerging treatments.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Primary bone cancers including osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, and chondrosarcoma are rare but require specialized treatment. Our team coordinates with orthopedic oncology surgeons to deliver neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy around surgical resection.

For patients with metastatic or recurrent bone cancers, we offer access to clinical trials and emerging therapies.

  • Fracture from weakened bone

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
Who gets bone cancer?

Osteosarcoma is most common in adolescents and young adults, while chondrosarcoma is more common in middle-aged adults. Ewing sarcoma primarily affects children and young adults.

Is limb salvage possible?

Yes. Most patients with extremity bone cancers can be treated with limb-salvage surgery rather than amputation, especially when chemotherapy shrinks the tumor before surgery.

title: Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes
description: Expert care for aplastic anemia, MDS, and other bone marrow failure conditions.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Bone marrow failure syndromes include myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), aplastic anemia, and related conditions where the bone marrow cannot produce enough healthy blood cells.

Our hematologists use advanced molecular diagnostics to classify these conditions and offer treatments including growth factors, immunosuppressive therapy, hypomethylating agents, and transplant coordination.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What is MDS?

Myelodysplastic syndromes are conditions where bone marrow produces abnormal blood cells. MDS can range from mild to severe and may progress to acute leukemia in some cases.

Is bone marrow transplant the only cure?

Stem cell transplant is the only curative option for many bone marrow failure syndromes, but not all patients are candidates. Other treatments can effectively manage the disease for years.

title: Brain Cancers
description: Advanced treatment for primary and metastatic brain tumors using radiation and systemic therapies.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Brain tumors — whether primary malignancies like gliomas or metastases from other cancers — require specialized, precise treatment. Our radiation oncologists offer stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and whole-brain radiation, while our medical oncologists manage systemic therapies tailored to the specific tumor type.

We coordinate closely with neurosurgeons and neuro-oncology specialists to develop comprehensive treatment plans that address both the tumor and quality of life.

sections.html:

  • Seizures (new onset)

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What is stereotactic radiosurgery?

SRS delivers highly focused radiation beams to a precise target in the brain, often completing treatment in a single session. Despite the name, it does not involve incisions — it is a non-invasive radiation technique.

Can brain metastases be treated?

Yes. Many patients with brain metastases from other cancers can be effectively treated with SRS, whole-brain radiation, or systemic therapies that cross the blood-brain barrier.

title: Breast Cancer Treatment
description: Personalized, multidisciplinary treatment plans combining advanced therapies and compassionate support for every stage of breast cancer.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers diagnosed in women, and with early detection and modern treatment, outcomes are better than ever. At Utah Cancer Specialists, our breast cancer program brings together medical oncologists, radiation oncologists, surgical partners, genetic counselors, and supportive-care specialists into a single coordinated team — so every patient receives a treatment plan built around her specific type, stage, and goals.

Whether you've just been diagnosed or are seeking a second opinion, our team will walk you through every step, explain your options in clear language, and help you make confident, informed decisions about your care.

1 in 8
U.S. women diagnosed in their lifetime
99%
5-year survival for localized disease
40+
Clinical trials available

sections.title: Symptoms & Early Warning Signs
sections.html:
Many breast cancers are found through routine screening before symptoms appear. When symptoms do occur, they can include:

  • A new lump or thickening in the breast or underarm
  • Changes in the size, shape, or contour of the breast
  • Skin changes such as dimpling, puckering, or redness
  • Nipple changes, including inversion, pain, or discharge
  • Unusual or persistent breast pain
  • Swelling or tenderness in the underarm lymph nodes

If you notice any of these changes, talk to your primary care provider or request a consultation directly with our team.

sections.title: Diagnosis & Staging
sections.html:
Accurate diagnosis and staging are the foundation of effective treatment. Our team uses a comprehensive workup that may include:

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
When should I start breast cancer screening?

Most guidelines recommend annual screening mammograms starting at age 40, though women with family history or genetic risk factors may need to begin earlier. We're happy to help you build a screening plan that's right for your personal history.

Will I need chemotherapy?

Not every patient needs chemotherapy. Modern genomic tests like Oncotype DX and MammaPrint help us determine which patients truly benefit — so many early-stage patients can safely avoid chemo and its side effects.

How do I get a second opinion?

We welcome second-opinion visits. Simply call 801.269.0231 to schedule; our team will help gather your records and imaging so the visit is productive from day one.

Do you offer clinical trials for breast cancer?

Yes. Through our START Program, patients have access to a growing portfolio of breast cancer clinical trials, including early-phase studies of novel targeted therapies and immunotherapy combinations.

Is genetic testing covered by insurance?

Most insurance plans cover genetic testing when clinical criteria are met. Our genetic counselors will walk you through the process and help verify coverage before testing.

title: Chronic Leukemias
description: Long-term management of chronic lymphocytic and chronic myeloid leukemias.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Chronic leukemias — including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) — are slow-growing blood cancers that often require long-term management rather than aggressive upfront treatment.

CML has been transformed by tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and CLL treatment has been revolutionized by BTK inhibitors and BCL-2 inhibitors. Our hematologists are experienced in selecting the right therapy and monitoring for optimal long-term outcomes.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
Does chronic leukemia always need treatment?

Not always. Many CLL patients are monitored with a 'watch and wait' approach until treatment criteria are met. CML typically requires treatment at diagnosis with a TKI.

Can CML be cured?

While most CML patients take TKI therapy long-term, some patients who achieve deep molecular remission may be eligible for treatment-free remission trials.

title: Clinical Trials (START Program)
description: Access to cutting-edge clinical trials and investigational treatments through the START Mountain Region program.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Utah Cancer Specialists has been committed to advancing cancer care through clinical research for more than 25 years. We manage over 50 active clinical trials at any given time, spanning all phases of development from early Phase I through Phase III.

Through the START Mountain Region program — established in 2020 and led by Dr. Justin Call — we offer Utah's only dedicated community-based early-phase clinical trial site, part of the world's largest Phase I medical oncology research program. Patients who have exhausted standard options or want access to the most novel therapies can explore trials right here in Utah.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What is a clinical trial?

A clinical trial is a carefully designed research study that tests new treatments in patients. All trials are reviewed by an Institutional Review Board (IRB) and participation is always voluntary.

Will I receive a placebo?

Most cancer clinical trials do not use placebos. When a placebo arm is included, patients always receive at least the current standard of care.

How do I find out if I'm eligible?

Contact our clinical research team at 801.907.4750 (START) or 801.281.6864 (UCS Trials), or ask your oncologist about trial options at your next visit.

title: Colon Cancer
description: Advanced colon cancer care with individualized treatment plans including surgery, chemotherapy, and targeted therapies.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer in the United States, but outcomes have improved significantly with modern screening, surgical techniques, and systemic therapies. Our team manages all stages from early-stage resectable disease through advanced metastatic colorectal cancer.

Molecular profiling — including MSI, RAS, BRAF, and HER2 testing — guides our treatment decisions, ensuring each patient receives the most effective targeted therapy or immunotherapy available.

  • Unexplained weight loss

  • Feeling that the bowel does not empty completely

What does MSI-high mean for my treatment?

MSI-high (microsatellite instability-high) tumors respond exceptionally well to immunotherapy, sometimes achieving durable remissions even in advanced disease.

title: Endocrine Tumors
description: Specialized treatment for adrenal, pituitary, and neuroendocrine tumors.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Endocrine tumors arise from hormone-producing tissues and include neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), adrenal cancers, pituitary tumors, and carcinoid tumors. These cancers often require specialized knowledge of both oncology and endocrinology.

Our team uses somatostatin receptor imaging (Gallium 68 DOTATATE PET) and targeted radionuclide therapy (Lutathera) alongside standard systemic treatments.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What is a neuroendocrine tumor?

NETs arise from neuroendocrine cells found throughout the body. They can be slow-growing (low-grade) or aggressive (high-grade) and may produce excess hormones.

What is Lutathera?

Lutathera (Lu-177 DOTATATE) is a targeted radionuclide therapy that delivers radiation directly to NET cells expressing somatostatin receptors.

title: Esophageal Cancer
description: Expert care combining chemotherapy, radiation, and advanced surgical techniques for esophageal cancer.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Esophageal cancer includes squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, each with distinct risk factors and treatment approaches. Our team uses a multimodal strategy combining chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery, with immunotherapy now playing an important role in advanced disease.

For locally advanced tumors, neoadjuvant chemoradiation followed by surgery is the standard approach, and our radiation oncologists use advanced techniques to minimize toxicity.

What is the role of immunotherapy?

Checkpoint inhibitors are now part of standard treatment for advanced esophageal cancer and are also being studied as part of neoadjuvant regimens.

title: Head & Neck Cancers
description: Multidisciplinary treatment for cancers of the throat, mouth, sinuses, and other head and neck regions.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Head and neck cancers include a diverse group of malignancies affecting the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, sinuses, and salivary glands. Treatment requires a carefully coordinated approach that balances cancer control with preservation of critical functions like speech, swallowing, and breathing.

Our radiation oncologists use advanced techniques like IMRT and IGRT to precisely target tumors while sparing surrounding healthy tissue, and our medical oncologists offer the latest immunotherapy and chemotherapy options.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs

  • Persistent sore throat or difficulty swallowing
  • A lump in the neck
  • Voice changes or hoarseness
  • Ear pain or hearing changes
  • Unexplained weight loss

Will treatment affect my ability to speak or eat?

Our team prioritizes function preservation. Advanced radiation techniques minimize impact on speech and swallowing, and we provide rehabilitation support throughout treatment.

title: Kidney Cancer
description: Specialized kidney cancer treatment combining immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and surgical options.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Kidney cancer, particularly renal cell carcinoma, has seen dramatic advances in treatment with immunotherapy and targeted drug combinations. Our team uses molecular profiling to select the optimal systemic therapy and coordinates closely with urologic surgeons for cases requiring surgical management.

For patients with metastatic disease, novel immunotherapy combinations have significantly improved outcomes, and we offer access to clinical trials testing the next generation of treatments.

What are TKI drugs?

Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are targeted drugs that block specific enzymes cancer cells need to grow. They are a cornerstone of advanced kidney cancer treatment, often combined with immunotherapy.

The introduction of immunotherapy-targeted therapy combinations has significantly improved outcomes in advanced HCC, and our practice offers access to these treatments along with clinical trials.

title: Lung Cancer
description: Comprehensive lung cancer care using the latest diagnostic tools and targeted therapies for the best possible outcomes.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Lung cancer remains one of the most common and serious cancers, but treatment has been transformed by advances in targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and precision radiation. At Utah Cancer Specialists, we use molecular profiling to identify the specific mutations driving your cancer, then match you with the most effective therapies available.

Whether your diagnosis is non-small cell, small cell, or a rare subtype, our multidisciplinary team develops an individualized treatment plan that combines the latest evidence with compassionate, whole-person care.

  • Unexplained weight loss and fatigue
  • Recurrent respiratory infections

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
Is lung cancer only caused by smoking?

No. While smoking is the leading risk factor, approximately 20% of lung cancer cases occur in people who have never smoked. Radon exposure, secondhand smoke, occupational chemicals, and genetic factors also play a role.

What is targeted therapy?

Targeted therapy uses drugs designed to attack specific genetic mutations in cancer cells. Molecular testing of your tumor identifies which mutations are present, allowing us to match you with FDA-approved targeted drugs or clinical trials.

Do you offer lung cancer screening?

Yes. We follow USPSTF guidelines recommending annual low-dose CT screening for adults aged 50-80 with a 20 pack-year smoking history. Talk to your primary care doctor or call us for a referral.

title: Lymphomas
description: Expert diagnosis and treatment for Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas using the latest immunotherapy and targeted approaches.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Lymphomas are cancers of the lymphatic system and represent one of the most treatable forms of cancer. Our hematology-oncology team specializes in both Hodgkin lymphoma and the many subtypes of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, using molecular classification to guide treatment selection.

Advances in immunotherapy, CAR-T cell coordination, and targeted agents have dramatically improved outcomes, and our practice offers access to the latest therapies through clinical trials and standard-of-care treatment.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Painless swollen lymph nodes in neck, armpit, or groin
  • Persistent fatigue
  • Unexplained fever and night sweats
  • Unintended weight loss
  • Itching without apparent cause
  • Cough or shortness of breath

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What is the difference between Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma?

Hodgkin lymphoma is characterized by the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells and typically follows a predictable pattern of spread. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is more diverse with over 60 subtypes, each with different behavior and treatment approaches.

Is lymphoma curable?

Many lymphomas are curable, especially Hodgkin lymphoma and certain aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Even indolent (slow-growing) lymphomas that may not be curable can often be managed effectively for many years.

title: Multiple Myeloma
description: Specialized treatment including novel immunotherapies and stem cell transplant support for multiple myeloma.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. Treatment has advanced dramatically in recent years with the introduction of proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, monoclonal antibodies, and bispecific antibodies.

Our team manages the full continuum of myeloma care — from smoldering myeloma surveillance through frontline treatment, transplant coordination, and management of relapsed disease.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Bone pain, especially in the spine or ribs
  • Fatigue and weakness
  • Frequent infections
  • Kidney problems or elevated calcium
  • Numbness or tingling in extremities

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
Is myeloma curable?

While myeloma is not yet considered curable for most patients, modern treatments have significantly extended survival. Many patients achieve deep remissions and live for years with good quality of life.

What is a stem cell transplant?

Autologous stem cell transplant uses your own stem cells collected before high-dose chemotherapy, then returned to rebuild your bone marrow. It remains a key treatment for eligible myeloma patients.

title: Myeloproliferative Disorders
description: Diagnosis and management of conditions where bone marrow produces too many blood cells.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are a group of blood disorders in which the bone marrow overproduces red blood cells, white blood cells, or platelets. Conditions include polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and myelofibrosis.

Our hematologists have extensive experience managing these chronic conditions, using targeted therapies like JAK inhibitors alongside careful monitoring to reduce complications and maintain quality of life.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Fatigue and weakness
  • Headaches or dizziness
  • Enlarged spleen (abdominal fullness)
  • Night sweats
  • Itching, especially after bathing
  • Blood clots or unusual bleeding

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
Are MPNs a type of cancer?

MPNs are classified as blood neoplasms (cancers), but many behave as chronic conditions that can be managed for years with appropriate treatment.

Can MPNs transform into leukemia?

There is a small risk of transformation to acute myeloid leukemia over time. Regular monitoring helps detect any changes early.

title: Ovarian Cancer
description: Advanced ovarian cancer treatment including surgery, chemotherapy, and emerging targeted approaches.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Ovarian cancer is often called a silent disease because early symptoms can be subtle. At Utah Cancer Specialists, we combine aggressive surgical and medical approaches with the latest targeted therapies and PARP inhibitors to give every patient the best possible outcome.

Our team includes medical oncologists experienced in gynecologic malignancies who work in coordination with surgical specialists and genetic counselors.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Bloating or abdominal swelling
  • Pelvic or abdominal pain
  • Difficulty eating or feeling full quickly
  • Urinary urgency or frequency
  • Unexplained fatigue or weight change

Should I get genetic testing?

We recommend genetic counseling for all ovarian cancer patients, as BRCA mutations and other hereditary factors affect treatment decisions and family screening recommendations.

What are PARP inhibitors?

PARP inhibitors are targeted drugs that block cancer cells from repairing their DNA, especially effective in patients with BRCA mutations or HRD-positive tumors.

title: Pancreatic & Gallbladder Cancer
description: Advanced care with multidisciplinary treatment planning for pancreatic and biliary cancers.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Pancreatic and gallbladder (biliary tract) cancers are among the most challenging malignancies to treat, but advances in chemotherapy combinations, targeted therapies, and clinical trials are improving outcomes.

Our medical oncologists work closely with surgeons, interventional radiologists, and palliative care specialists to provide comprehensive treatment at every stage of disease.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Jaundice (yellowing of skin and eyes)
  • Abdominal or back pain
  • Unexplained weight loss
  • Loss of appetite
  • New-onset diabetes
  • Dark urine or pale stools

Is pancreatic cancer treatable?

While pancreatic cancer remains challenging, modern chemotherapy regimens and clinical trials have improved survival. Some patients with resectable tumors achieve long-term remission after surgery and adjuvant therapy.

What role does genetic testing play?

Up to 10% of pancreatic cancers have actionable mutations like BRCA. Germline and somatic testing can identify patients eligible for PARP inhibitors and other targeted therapies.

title: Prostate Cancer
description: Expert, evidence-based prostate cancer treatment focused on preserving quality of life and long-term health.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men, but when caught early, it is also one of the most treatable. At Utah Cancer Specialists, our team uses a personalized approach that considers the stage and grade of your cancer, your age, overall health, and personal preferences to develop a treatment plan tailored specifically to you.

From active surveillance for low-risk disease to advanced radiation and systemic therapies for aggressive cancers, we provide the full spectrum of prostate cancer care — always with an emphasis on preserving quality of life.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• Difficulty urinating or weak urine flow
  • Frequent urination, especially at night
  • Blood in urine or semen
  • Pain or discomfort in the pelvic area
  • Bone pain (in advanced stages)
  • Erectile dysfunction

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
When should I start screening?

Most guidelines recommend discussing PSA screening with your doctor starting at age 50, or at 40-45 if you have risk factors such as family history or African American heritage.

What is active surveillance?

For low-risk prostate cancer, active surveillance means closely monitoring the cancer with regular PSA tests, imaging, and biopsies rather than treating immediately — avoiding side effects while ensuring the cancer doesn't progress.

Will treatment affect my quality of life?

Modern treatment approaches are designed to minimize side effects. Our team discusses potential impacts on urinary, bowel, and sexual function and works with you to choose the approach that best balances cancer control with quality of life.

title: Rectal Cancer
description: Specialized treatment with multimodal approaches including radiation, chemotherapy, and surgery.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Rectal cancer treatment has evolved significantly, with many patients now receiving neoadjuvant (pre-surgical) chemotherapy and radiation to shrink tumors before surgery. Our team coordinates a multimodal approach that maximizes the chance of organ preservation when possible.

For some patients with complete clinical response to neoadjuvant therapy, a watch-and-wait approach may be considered, avoiding major surgery altogether.

Why is treatment different from colon cancer?

Rectal cancer's proximity to the anal sphincter and other structures requires specialized radiation and surgical techniques to achieve the best cancer control while preserving function.

What is total neoadjuvant therapy?

TNT delivers all chemotherapy and radiation before surgery, which can improve outcomes and increase the chance of a complete pathologic response.

title: Small Bowel Cancers
description: Specialized treatment for rare cancers of the small intestine.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Small bowel cancers are rare and include adenocarcinomas, neuroendocrine tumors, lymphomas, and sarcomas. Due to their rarity, these cancers benefit from the expertise of an experienced oncology team familiar with the nuances of each subtype.

Our team tailors treatment based on tumor type and location, coordinating surgery, systemic therapy, and supportive care.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs

  • Unexplained weight loss

sections.html:
How are small bowel cancers diagnosed?

Due to their location, small bowel cancers can be challenging to diagnose. CT enterography and capsule endoscopy are important diagnostic tools.

Are treatment options different from colon cancer?

Yes. Treatment depends on the specific subtype — adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine, lymphoma, or sarcoma — each requiring a different approach.

title: Soft Tissue Cancers (Sarcomas)
description: Expert sarcoma treatment for cancers in muscle, fat, nerves, and connective tissues.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Soft tissue sarcomas are rare cancers that can arise in muscle, fat, blood vessels, nerves, and connective tissues anywhere in the body. With over 50 subtypes, expert pathologic classification is essential for treatment planning.

Our team coordinates with orthopedic and surgical oncologists for limb-sparing surgery when possible, and uses radiation and chemotherapy tailored to the specific sarcoma subtype.

sections.title: Symptoms & Warning Signs
sections.html:
• A growing lump or mass in the body
  • Pain if the tumor presses on nerves
  • Swelling in an arm or leg
  • Abdominal fullness or pain

sections.html:
Are sarcomas different from other cancers?

Yes. Sarcomas arise from connective tissues rather than epithelial tissues (where carcinomas originate). They require specialized pathologic classification and treatment approaches.

Is limb amputation necessary?

Modern surgical techniques and radiation therapy allow limb-sparing surgery for the majority of extremity sarcomas.

title: Stomach Cancer
description: Comprehensive gastric cancer treatment including targeted therapy and immunotherapy.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Stomach (gastric) cancer requires a multidisciplinary approach combining surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. Our team uses HER2 testing and PD-L1 assessment to identify patients who will benefit from the latest targeted and immune-based treatments.

We manage all stages from early resectable disease through advanced metastatic gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancers.

title: Thyroid Cancer
description: Expert care with specialized surgical, radioactive iodine, and targeted therapy options for thyroid cancer.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Thyroid cancer is one of the most curable cancers when detected early. Our team works closely with endocrinologists and surgeons to provide a complete treatment pathway from diagnosis through long-term surveillance.

For more advanced or aggressive thyroid cancers, we offer targeted therapies, radioactive iodine treatment coordination, and access to clinical trials with novel agents.

  • Difficulty swallowing or breathing
  • Persistent hoarseness or voice changes
  • Neck or throat pain
  • Swollen lymph nodes in the neck

Most thyroid cancers have an excellent prognosis. The 5-year survival rate for localized papillary and follicular thyroid cancer is over 99%.

Will I need to take medication after treatment?

Most patients require lifelong thyroid hormone replacement after surgery, which also helps suppress any remaining cancer cells.

title: Uterine Cancer

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Uterine cancer, including endometrial cancer, is the most common gynecologic malignancy. Early detection leads to excellent outcomes, and our team offers the full range of treatment options from surgery through advanced systemic therapies.

We coordinate closely with gynecologic surgeons and radiation specialists to ensure each patient receives a comprehensive, individualized treatment plan.

What are the risk factors?

Risk factors include obesity, diabetes, hormone replacement therapy, late menopause, and Lynch syndrome. Regular gynecologic exams help with early detection.

Is surgery always required?

Surgery is the primary treatment for most uterine cancers, but for patients who are not surgical candidates, radiation and systemic therapy can be effective alternatives.
